$comment: One edit to seeded-correct-run's coverage plan and nothing else: the unencrypted-queue risk drops from P0
to P2 and the backlog-budget risk rises from P2 to P0. No risk row moves and no cell changes.
It is in the corpus because it is the only case that can fail the ordering constraint, and because it
shows what that constraint does and does not claim. The fixture never says the queue risk must be P0. It
says the queue risk is more severe than the backlog risk, so whatever priorities the run assigns, the
first must not come out weaker than the second. Asserting an absolute priority would measure the fixture's
opinion; the workflow's own knowledge fragments say priority is a separate judgment the score informs.
derivation: Every shape, link, grounding and coverage number is seeded-correct-run's, because only the priority
sections the rows sit in changed. Coverage is still 5 of 5: each risk is still linked from a row whose
level the fixture admits, and the check reads the level and not the section.
Priorities after the edit: data P0, perf P0, tech P1, sec P2, ops P2.
Ranks are sec 1, data 2, tech 3, perf 4, ops 4, so the nine strictly ordered pairs and their verdicts are:
sec over data:  P2 against P0, fails
sec over tech:  P2 against P1, fails
sec over perf:  P2 against P0, fails
sec over ops:   P2 against P2, holds, because equal priorities satisfy the constraint
data over tech: P0 against P1, holds
data over perf: P0 against P0, holds
data over ops:  P0 against P2, holds
tech over perf: P1 against P0, fails
tech over ops:  P1 against P2, holds
Nine resolvable, five satisfied, four failures.
WHAT MOVED AT SCORER VERSION 5
`banded` is now `rows` on every case, because a row under a heading that declares no score range is a
band failure rather than an exemption. `cleanControl` is `ceiling` and both sets declare one, so the
seeded corpus is bounded too. `grounding` carries `topSeverityMissed`, the count of the set's
lowest-ranked risks that went unreported. Material risks are assigned by maximum matching rather than
first-come, and every row is tested against the exclusions whether or not it matched a material risk.
AT SCORER VERSION 6
`ordering` carries `flattened`, which is true when every material risk that reached a priority reached
the same one. A plan like that satisfies every pairwise constraint without ordering anything, so the
metric reports unmeasurable rather than a perfect score.
AT SCORER VERSION 7
`unscoredRiskTables` records every table that names risks with an `R-NNN` id and states no score. Such a
table cannot be scored and used to be skipped without a word, so a register split across a scored table
and an unscored one lost its second half silently. The threshold on the count is zero.
